penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Solo freelancers paying $20-40/mo means you need hundreds of customers to reach meaningful revenue; the model only works at consumer scale.

rationale: The buyer here is a cost-sensitive solo freelancer who wants to avoid monthly subscriptions — this is structurally the worst buyer for a subscription product, and their WTP ceiling is the very thing they're complaining about. Even if buildable as a Claude-powered automation layer, the buyer clarity is too weak: 'freelancers' is a large, fragmented audience with no specific budget line, and the core objection is that existing tools already charge too little. The b2c_at_scale penalty pushes the total below the validate threshold, confirming this is not viable at solo-operator scale.
solution_plan: Not recommended to pursue. The target buyer's defining trait is resistance to subscription costs, so any recurring-fee product faces immediate churn. A one-time tool would need a very large install base to generate meaningful revenue, requiring marketing scale a solo non-technical operator cannot achieve without significant paid acquisition spend. If the idea were to be validated anyway, the factory could build a simple Claude-powered outreach workflow template sold as a one-time Gumroad product, but the economics are unlikely to work.
notes: Fails buyer_clarity_min (4 < 6) and willingness_to_pay_min (4 < 5) build gates. Total also below validate threshold after penalty.
